deed: Hezekiah, King of Judah, and his hewers cut the Siloam Tunnel and brought water into Jerusalem
title: Hezekiah, King of Judah, and his hewers cut a tunnel through the rock and brought water into Jerusalem

trailer.text: Hezekiah was King of Judah, and according to Science News he reigned from 727 to 698 BCE.
According to a press release on the study, a half-kilometer tunnel was cut through the rock on his initiative, without intermediate shafts.
According to the announcement, the tunnel brought water to Jerusalem and protected the water during the Assyrian siege of Sancherib in 701 B.C.E.
In 2003, Amos Frumkin of the Hebrew University, Aryeh Shimron of the Geological Survey of Israel and Jeff Rosenbaum of Reading University published a dating of the tunnel in Nature.
According to Science News, they found that the tunnel was probably built around 700 BCE, which supports the Bible verses that attribute it to Hezekiah.

stations.title: Before: the Gihon Spring and the Assyrian threat

paragraphs.text: According to an article by Asher Grossberg, in the First Temple period two water systems carried the waters of the Gihon Spring to the pool at the end of Jerusalem's central valley.
Second Chronicles describes how Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, intending to make war against Jerusalem.

According to Grossberg, the prevailing view, which is almost undisputed, attributes to the hewing of the Siloam Tunnel the description at the end of chapter 32 of Chronicles, of Hezekiah blocking the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon.
According to Science News, Hezekiah reigned from 727 to 698 BCE, while BAR gives the years 727–697 BCE.
According to the press release on the study, a simpler method, used for thousands of years, was based on digging vertical shafts from the surface.
According to the press release, the half-kilometer Siloam Tunnel was cut without intermediate shafts, which was an engineering innovation in its time.
According to the Nature article, it is one of the longest ancient tunnels cut without intermediate shafts.
According to the researchers Frumkin and Shimron, the tunnel points to an advance in leveling techniques.
According to them, this advance was essential for cutting such a long tunnel without intermediate shafts.
The researchers also state that geological, structural and chemical features show that it is an authentic engineering project, and that there was no natural fissure there to guide the hewers.
According to Grossberg, the Siloam Tunnel is approximately three times as long as the southern part of the Siloam Channel.
According to him, its hewing volume is approximately six times greater.

stations.title: Two teams meet inside the rock

paragraphs.text: According to the researchers, two hewing teams finally met inside the rock.
According to them, the winding route of the tunnel and the final meeting are linked to continuous changes in the plan.
The purpose of the changes was to allow voice communication between the hewers and the teams on the surface.
According to the researchers, hydraulic plaster was applied along the entire tunnel.
The plaster sealed cavities formed by dissolution and by tectonic processes.
According to BAR, an ancient inscription discovered in 1880 describes the construction of the tunnel.
According to the press release, the Siloam inscription is kept in a museum in Istanbul, and it does not say who built the tunnel.
According to Grossberg, the inscription does not mention any king of Judah.
According to BAR, the tunnel winds about a third of a mile south, from the Gihon Spring to the Siloam Pool.
According to the press release, it brought water into Jerusalem and protected this resource during the Assyrian siege in 701 BCE, led by Sennacherib.
According to Grossberg, the hewing was a large and complex project, and its completion required several years.
According to him, the work began even before Sennacherib's siege.
According to Grossberg, after Sennacherib's defeat Hezekiah decided to complete the tunnel, probably because the work was at an advanced stage.
According to the press release, the Siloam Tunnel is one of the oldest structures still in use today.
According to a 2006 article in the Journal of Archaeological Science, it is the best-identified biblical structure that can be entered today.
According to Science News, a team led by geologist Amos Frumkin of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem entered the dispute over the tunnel's date.
According to the press release, Dr. Aryeh Shimron of the Geological Survey of Israel and Dr. Jeff Rosenbaum of Reading University in England also took part in the study.
Frumkin said that until then the assumption that the tunnel dated from Hezekiah's time rested only on the biblical text and on the inscription found in the tunnel itself.
The researchers carbon-14 dated fragments of wood and plants that were accidentally trapped in the plaster with which the original builders coated the tunnel.
According to Physics World, the measurements were made with an accelerator mass spectrometer at Oxford University.
According to Physics World, the measurements showed that the material in the plaster dates from between about 800 and 510 BCE.
According to Physics World, stalactites from the tunnel's ceiling were dated by uranium-thorium at the Open University in the UK.
According to Physics World, the stalactites were found to be more than 2300 years old.
According to Science News, these measurements indicate that the passage was built before 300 BCE.
According to Physics World, the researchers calculated that the tunnel was built around 700 BCE.
The findings were published in Nature, in the September 11, 2003 issue.
Frumkin told PhysicsWeb that this is the first time a structure mentioned in the Bible has been radiometrically dated.
According to the article's abstract, until then no well-identified biblical structure had been radiometrically dated.

stations.title: What the dating said about the dispute

paragraphs.text: According to Science News, some scholars accepted the biblical account of the tunnel's construction, and others argued otherwise.
According to Science News, scholars who opposed the biblical dating argued that the inscriptions at the tunnel's exit indicate hewing between 200 and 100 BCE.
According to BAR, some scholars argued that the inscription dates to the second century BCE, a claim that most scholars firmly rejected.
According to the Nature article, the dating refutes the claim that the tunnel was built in the second century BCE.
According to the authors, the dating proved that the tunnel dates to Iron Age II.
From this the authors concluded that the biblical text is an accurate historical record of its construction.
According to Frumkin and Shimron, the dating supports the evidence attributing the engineering advance in tunneling to Hezekiah, King of Judah.
According to Grossberg, the radiometric dating of the pieces of wood and plants from the plaster does not make it possible to decide between the different views on when the tunnel was hewn.
According to Grossberg, some scholars attribute the tunnel to Manasseh rather than to Hezekiah, among them Sneh, Weinberger and Shalev.
According to Makor Rishon, Prof. Gershon Galil of the University of Haifa claims that he and his colleague Eli Shukron discovered five additional inscriptions in the tunnel and its surroundings.
Galil claims that the inscriptions state the date the tunnel was completed: the 17th year of Hezekiah, which is 709 BCE.
According to him, one of the inscriptions was carved in the rock to the right of the entrance to Channel No. 4, in the round chamber in the Canaanite pool near the Gihon Spring.
According to Galil, Father Vincent located the inscription's frame in 1909, but believed there was only a frame there and no inscription.
Galil also claims that an examination of the original Siloam inscription in Istanbul revealed that two more lines are inscribed on it.
He claims that the inscriptions support the argument that the Book of Kings is based on chronicles and royal inscriptions.
According to Makor Rishon, in academic circles Galil's publication is being received with a certain skepticism.
Archaeologist Gabi Barkay said he had not seen anything that would convince him that it is true.
Barkay said it is necessary to wait for a scientific publication and better photographs that will clarify what exists there.

claims.quote: Being one of the longest ancient water tunnels lacking intermediate shafts, dating the Siloam Tunnel is a key to determining where and when this technological breakthrough took place.

claims.text: לפי Science News, חוקרים שהתנגדו לתיארוך המקראי טענו שהכתובות ביציאת הנקבה מצביעות על תאריך חציבה בין 200 ל-100 לפנה"ס.
claims.quote: indicated an excavation date between 200 B.C. and 100 B.C.

claims.text: לפי BAR, חלק מהחוקרים טענו שהכתובת מהמאה השנייה לפנה"ס, טענה שרוב החוקרים דחו בתוקף.
claims.quote: Some scholars have argued that the Siloam Tunnel inscription dated to the second century B.C., a claim roundly disputed by most scholars.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, תיארוך הנקבה מפריך טענה שלפיה היא נבנתה במאה השנייה לפנה"ס.
claims.quote: Siloam Tunnel dating also refutes a claim that the tunnel was constructed in the second century BC.

claims.text: לפי Physics World, החוקרים הסיקו שהנקבה לא נבנתה מאוחר כמו המאה ה-2 לפנה"ס, כפי שמאמינים חלק מהארכיאולוגים.
claims.quote: They therefore conclude that the tunnel could not have been built as late as the 2nd century BC, as some archaeologists believe.

claims.text: במאמר ב-Nature דווח על תיארוך פחמן-14 ואורניום-תוריום של נקבת השילוח, שהוכיח לדברי המחברים כי היא מתקופת הברזל ב', והם הסיקו שהטקסט המקראי הוא תיעוד היסטורי מדויק של בניית הנקבה.
claims.quote: Here we report radiocarbon and U-Th dating of the Siloam Tunnel, proving its Iron Age II date; we conclude that the Biblical text presents an accurate historic record of the Siloam Tunnel's construction.

claims.text: לפי גרוסברג, התיארוך הרדיומטרי של חתיכות עץ וצמחים מהטיח של הנקבה אינו מאפשר להכריע בין הדעות השונות על מועד חציבתה.
claims.quote: אינו מאפשר להכריע בין הדעות השונות, 2003 חתיכות עץ וצמחים שנמצאו בטיח של נקבת השילוח

claims.text: לפי גרוסברג, יש חוקרים (סנה, ויינברגר ושלו) המשייכים את נקבת השילוח למנשה ולא לחזקיהו.
claims.quote: שמשייכים את נקבת השילוח למנשה, ומאמרם של רייך ושוקרון

claims.text: לפי מקור ראשון, פרופ' גרשון גליל מאוניברסיטת חיפה טוען שהוא ועמיתו אלי שוקרון גילו בנקבת השילוח ובסביבתה חמש כתובות נוספות.
claims.quote: כי הוא ועמיתו הארכיאולוג אלי שוקרון גילו בנקבת השילוח ובסביבתה חמש כתובות נוספות

claims.text: לפי מקור ראשון, לטענת גליל הכתובות החדשות נוקבות בתאריך השלמת הנקבה: שנת 17 לחזקיהו, היא שנת 709 לפנה"ס.
claims.quote: בשנת 17 לחזקיהו, היא שנת 709 לפני הספירה

claims.text: לדברי גליל, אחת הכתובות נחקקה בסלע מימין לכניסה לתעלה מספר 4 בחדר העגול בבריכה הכנענית הסמוכה למעיין הגיחון.
claims.quote: נחקקה בסלע מימין לכניסה לתעלה מספר 4 בחדר העגול, המצוי בבריכה הכנענית הסמוכה למעיין הגיחון

claims.text: לפי גליל, את מסגרת הכתובת איתר האב וינסאן ב-1909, אך הוא סבר שאין שם כתובת אלא רק מסגרת.
claims.quote: את המסגרת של הכתובת איתר אומנם בשנת 1909 האב וינסאן, אך הוא סבר שאין שם כתובת אלא רק מסגרת

claims.text: גליל טוען שבבדיקת כתובת השילוח המקורית שבאיסטנבול התברר שרשומות עליה עוד שתי שורות.
claims.quote: מתברר שעל האבן המצויה באיסטנבול רשומות עוד שתי שורות

claims.text: גליל טוען שהכתובות מסייעות לטענה שספר מלכים מבוסס על כרוניקות וכתובות מלכותיות.
claims.quote: הוא הוסיף והסביר שהכתובות מסייעות לטענה שהכתוב בספר מלכים מבוסס על טקסטים שמקורם בכרוניקות ובכתובות מלכותיות

claims.text: לפי מקור ראשון, בחוגים אקדמיים מקבלים את הפרסום של גליל בפקפוק מסוים.
claims.quote: אלא שבחוגים האקדמיים העוסקים בעניין מקבלים את הפרסום השבוע בפקפוק מסוים

claims.text: הארכיאולוג גבי ברקאי הגיב לפרסום של גליל ושוקרון שלא ראה דבר שישכנע אותו שהדבר נכון.
claims.quote: לא ראיתי עוד שום דבר שישכנע אותי שזה נכון

claims.text: ברקאי אמר שצריך לחכות לפרסום מדעי ולתמונות טובות יותר שיבהירו מה קיים שם.
claims.quote: צריך לחכות לפרסום מדעי ולתמונות טובות יותר שיבהירו מה קיים שם

claims.text: לפי גרוסברג, הדעה הרווחת, שכמעט אין עליה עוררין, מייחסת לחציבת נקבת השילוח את התיאור שבסוף פרק לב בדברי הימים, על סתימת מוצא מימי גיחון העליון.
claims.quote: בתיאור שבסוף פרק לב בספר דברי הימים נזכר מעיין הגיחון
